## TL;DR

I drove the auth-less dev server at 375 and 768 CSS pixels across twelve main routes, in light and dark themes (48 page loads), and measured horizontal overflow and off-viewport controls. Those measurements found no overflow on any route. The real problems were in the tablet band of 720–900px, where the layout switches to the 60px icon rail. There I found three clipped or overlapping regions and fixed them in `style.css`: the Settings tab strip clipped its last tab between 761 and about 815px, the rail's theme switcher and build widget spilled past the rail edge, and the Work parked-toggle dock overlapped the Active column and the integration pill. I added a WebKit geometry test file with nine cases; five fail on the original CSS and all nine pass now. The QA record is `docs/qa/2026-11-web-mobile-widths.md`. I did not change the floating-avatar overlap on Settings, because its default placement is a product decision.

## Work and rationale

The spec asked for a pass at 375 and 768 across Work, Releases, Settings, Agents and Checks, plus a committed findings file. #1157 had already covered 390 and 320 and fixed a set of phone problems. I therefore kept the pass to 375 and 768, and I left #1157's fixes alone.

The first step was a measurement script, kept outside the tree and copied to `.repoos/qa/1170/`. For each route it records document `scrollWidth` against the viewport, and every visible element whose box passes the viewport edge, excluding elements inside a horizontal scroller on purpose. The script surfaced one offender, the Settings `repoos.toml` tab at x=781 in a 768 viewport. Screenshots found two more issues the box check cannot see: the rail's theme chips and build hash, and the Work toggles stacked over a card.

For the Settings strip, the cause was a breakpoint. The scroller rule ran only up to 760px, but the seven tabs need about 695px, and the container is about 656px at 768px. I measured the strip's natural width across widths and moved the breakpoint to 900px, which covers the whole rail band with margin. I did not rewrite the strip, because the existing scroller already hides its scrollbar and keeps the phone behaviour.

For the rail, the rule hiding `.theme-switch` and `.build-widget` used a single-class selector. Two base rules later in the file set `display: flex` with the same specificity, so the later rule won. Scoping the hide to `.sidebar` fixes it, and I left the other selectors in that list alone.

For the Work dock, the fixed toggle row assumed the 210px labelled sidebar, and its width formula reserved 520px for the centred integration pill. At 768px that left about 12px, so "Human (11)" wrapped and the chips covered the Active column. I considered two options. Moving the toggles into document flow would have placed them after the board, which is off-screen in this full-height layout. So I kept the fixed dock, set its left edge at the 60px rail, and lifted it above the pill. I also confirmed that the column end inset already clears the lifted row: at scroll end, the last Active card ends about 50px above the toggles.

## Approaches tried

I first tried a `networkidle` navigation wait. The Work route never went idle at 768, because of its live stream, so I switched to a `load` wait plus a fixed settle time. My first attempt at a regression test also asserted measured overflow on the Settings strip. It passed on the original CSS, because the test fixture's tab buttons measure about 40px narrower than the live app's, so the strip never overflowed in the fixture. I replaced that assertion with a check on the scroller rule, and I called that trade-off out in the test and in the QA record. I then confirmed the other four failing cases by swapping in the HEAD copy of `style.css`, running the tests, and restoring my version.

## Challenges and blockers

The auth-less server builds only when `just serve-noauth` runs from the worktree, and my first background launch died during the UI build. I ran `bun run build` in the foreground to get the real error. The build passed, and I then started `dist/cli/index.js serve --preview-overrides` directly with `REPOOS_PREVIEW_CHILD=1`, which is what the recipe runs. I did not start `repoos serve` myself.

Settings and Releases stayed on loading skeletons. Several API calls return access-control 401s in the no-auth session, so the Settings forms and the Releases cut panel were not seen at either width. This is a limit of the environment and not a finding, and the QA record says so. Real devices and touch were not available, so this pass covers layout geometry only.

Floating avatars cover the rightmost theme star buttons on Settings at 768px. The heads default to visible from 720px and are draggable, so this is a product decision about their default placement. I did not change it, and I flagged it in the QA record for a human decision.

The 901–1000px band still uses the desktop dock, which reserves 520px for the pill. That band is outside this task's widths, and I did not measure it. It is a candidate follow-up.

## Key learnings

Breakpoints that were correct when a layout had a 210px sidebar go wrong once a band switches to the 60px rail. Hard-coded sidebar offsets and reservations need to move with the rail, or they leak into the band. The same lesson applies to hiding elements: a single-class `display: none` in a media query loses to a later base rule with equal specificity, so scope the hide to its container.

A geometry test in WebKit with the real shared CSS catches these bugs where jsdom cannot. A fixture is only as good as its metrics, though: the Settings strip fixture measured narrower than the live app, so its overflow assertion passed on the original CSS. Where a fixture cannot reproduce the live metrics, assert the rule that guarantees the behaviour and say so.
